profile.headline: Junior Software Engineer at Uplevel
profile.summary: I'm a recent university graduate in the Seattle area with my Bachelor's of Science in Computer Science and Game Design. My dream is to one day work on games as my career, and I've prepared for this with my studies. I have four years of experience working on multi-disciplinary game teams with other students, one of which included developing a game in our own custom engine. I have 6 years of experience with C/C++/C# and Unity, and while developing my team's custom engine I learned to use libraries such as OpenGL and RapidJSON. Working on teams has also given me a lot of experience with version control, having used both SVN and Git in my projects. I am excited to hear about any full- or part-time job offers anywhere from indie/startup projects to AAA roles :)

positions.title: Junior Software Engineer
positions.description: I worked in Unity to create an app demo for Tradespark, working with tools like Modal and Supabase to deploy and quickly test our app's features. Most of my work went into the user login pipeline, allowing users to create a free account, log in anonymously, log into an existing account, upgrade their account to a paid subscription, or log out at any point seamlessly. I also helped implement location services and Google's Map Tiles API in a scene that would allow user's to view their current location as a sort of "dollhouse" they could edit.

positions.description: For the 2024-2025 school year, I was a part of DigiPen's Student Union (DSU), taking on the role of Vice President of Internal Affairs. This was an elected position, which I was referred for by campus staff. I planned and ran many of the large student events on campus throughout the school year, like the Halloween Carnival and Prom. I also worked with the rest of the DSU team to make important decisions regarding budget use, improving student life on campus, and making student voices heard.

positions.title: Open World Production Staff
positions.description:
I worked on the production staff over the summer for DigiPen's Open World K-12 camp program. I collaborated with multiple teams to keep the camp running smoothly, and my daily duties included:

- Planning/Running short engaging activities tailored to each age group during the students' breaks
- Monitoring Microsoft Teams in order to support teachers in their classrooms whenever necessary
- Delegating tasks to others on my team and making sure everything was done
- Communicating with the students' parents before after each day during pick-up
- Keeping the students safe by enforcing and demonstrating camp rules
- Cleaning up the main break room after each break, day, and camp session
- Making connections with the students to give them a fun and memorable camp experience

positions.title: Instructor
positions.description:
I worked with a team of other instructors for two months over the summer, teaching and engaging children for 8 hours a day every weekday. Each week, we also wrote individualized diplomas for each student in our class, highlighting their achievements throughout the week and congratulating them. Personally, I taught various technology-focused courses to children of ages 10-17 during this time, including the following subjects:

- 3D Printing and Modeling
- Art and Animation with Adobe Photoshop/Animate/Premier Pro
- Entrepreneurship
- Lua Coding with Roblox
- Game Design with Roblox
positions.insights: Skills: Teamwork · Game Development · Team Leadership · Adobe Photoshop · Game Design · Leadership · 3D Printing · Teaching · Customer Service

positions.description:
During my time at Bridges, I gained an abundance of knowledge on cat, dog, small animal, reptile, and fish care, as well as the pros and cons of associated products for these pets. Some of the main tasks I performed in this position include:

- Customer Service
- Running the Cash Registers
- Cleaning and Maintaining the Store
- Calling upon Coworkers when Necessary

projects.title: Cats & Critters: A Dungeon Claw-er
projects.description:
Cats & Critters: A Dungeon Claw-er is a 1-4 player party game where players take on the role of a group of intrepid cat wizards on an adventure to take back their stolen golden yarn from the great dragon Frank.

I created this project in Unity on a team of 9 students over the course of two semesters. The attached video and screenshots showcase the state of the project at the end of the school year (April 2024), but we intend to continue working on it throughout the summer to polish it and eventually release it to Steam and the DigiPen Game Gallery.

My main work in the game involved core multiplayer features like reviving allies, bubbling when players move too far from each other (similarly to the Mario series), and customizing characters to look distinct from each other. As far as backend work goes, I created singleton PartyInfo and PlayerInfo classes to hold important information that made implementing telemetry and enemy AI much easier for my other team members. Earlier on in the project, I also worked with another team member to set up the enemy AI framework, giving them the ability to sense nearby players and follow them.

Finally, I also took on the role of Co-Producer for the latter half of this project, assisting our producer with documentation and task management. We used ClickUp to track each member's individual tasks, and a spreadsheet to track our asset list for things like audio and art.

projects.title: Strike Back
projects.description:
Strike Back is a two-player fighting game with characters based on real-life martial arts from around the world. I created this game in a team of 19 students over the course of a year, mainly helping work on the custom engine it used. 

I worked on this project as a programmer during my sophomore year of DigiPen on a multi-disciplinary team with designers, artists, musicians, and other programmers.My main work on the project included researching JSON serialization and deserialization, implementing it with RapidJSON and later, JSON for Modern C++ by Niels Lohmann. I also worked with OpenGL for our game's graphics, and we created a robust editor with Dear ImGui. Lastly, I spent most of the latter half of the project working with our VFX artist to bring their vision for the game to life.

We published this game to the DigiPen Game Gallery after we finished the project at the end of the year; if you're interested in playing it,you can download it at https://games.digipen.edu/games/strike-back.

organizations.name: Future Business Leaders of America (FBLA)
organizations.description: I was a member of FBLA throughout all four years of high school, and held officer positions in my sophomore and senior years as the Public Relations Officer and President of our local chapter respectively. Throughout my time in this organization, I received many awards and honors; I placed in numerous competitions at both the Regional and State levels, and I qualified for the National level of competition two years in a row.
